1.    Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited.

The Applicant, South County Eden Operations LLC (“South County” or “Applicant”) a newly
formed entity wholly owned by Mr. Louis “Josh” Gellis, seeks Change in Effective Control (“CEC”)
approval for the acquisition of the 120 bed nursing home duly licensed and operated by South County
SNF Operations LLC (the “Current Operator”) located at 740 Oak Hill Road, North Kingstown,
Rhode Island (the “Facility”).

Pursuant to the terms of an Asset Purchase Agreement effective January 6, 2022, 780 Oak Hill Road
Eden Realty LLC (“Oak Hill Real Estate”), a Rhode Island limited liability company, purchased the
Facility real estate (the “Property”) from 780 Oak Hill Road SNF Real Estate LLC (see Tab 14). In
addition, subject to CEC approval and pursuant to the terms of an Operations Transfer Agreement
(“OTA”) entered into December 20, 2021, the Old Operator will assign and convey to the New
Operator the operating assets (see Tab 14). The closing on the Property occurred on March 2, 2022.
The closing on the operations will occur upon receipt of CEC approval.

The total purchase price for the acquisition of operations and real estate is Fourteen Million Dollars
($14,000,000) plus $360,000 in closing costs. The Applicant anticipates that it will fund the purchase
price with $11,280,000 in debt (80%) and $2,720,000 in equity (20%).

Mr. Gellis has a proven track record in Rhode Island as well as outside of the State in owning and
operating skilled nursing facilities. In Rhode Island, Mr. Gellis has an ownership and operator
interest in West View Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, a 120 bed duly licensed skilled nursing
facility in West Warwick, Rhode Island, Cortland Place Rehab Center LLC, d/b/a Stillwater
Assisted Living and Skilled Nursing Community an 80 bed duly licensed skilled nursing facility in
Greenville, Rhode Island, and Overlook Nursing and Rehabilitation Center, a 100 bed duly licensed
skilled nursing facility in Pascoag, Rhode Island. Mr. Gellis has also submitted Change in Effective
Control applications for the acquisition of Brentwood Health Center and Sunny View Nursing
Home, Inc, which are currently under review. In addition, Mr. Gellis, through 4040 Post Road
Eden Operations LLC, is the operator of Brentwood By the Bay, a licensed assisted living facility.
Mr. Gellis also has ownership interests in Delmar Nursing & Rehabilitation in Delmar, Delaware
and Rosewood Rehabilitation and Nursing Center in Rensselaer, New York. All of the facilities are
in good standing and are proud of the quality services provided to all residents.

within and outside Rhode Island) within the past three years, please demonstrate the record of that

Nursing facilities managed and/or owned by the Applicant’s owner have an excellent track record
with respect to access to traditionally underserved populations. In particular, skilled nursing
facilities in Rhode Island (West View, Stillwater, and Overlook), New York and Delaware provide
charity care services to residents qualified under applicable regulations and policies and also
provide services to Medicaid and Medicare residents.

17. Please identify the proposed immediate and long-term plans of the applicant to ensure adequate and
appropriate access to the program and health care services to be provided by the health care facility/ies to
traditionally underserved populations.

The Applicant will provide charity care pursuant to its Charity Care Policy (see Tab 18). In
addition, the Applicant will comply with all non-discrimination policies and procedures required
for Medicare certification, including, without limitation, those pertaining to residents with limited
English proficiency. Lastly the Applicant will provide services to both Medicare and Medicaid
residents.

         The Applicant will have sufficient funds available for capital and operating needs as

         evidence of 30 days operating expenses set forth in Appendix C, to ensure financial stability.
         The Applicant’s financial capability is strong as evidenced by the successful operation of

         All of the above referenced factors demonstrate the Applicant’s financial condition and its
         financial capability to operate the Facility.

included in the RUG schedule prepared by the Medicaid Office. The Medicaid Managed Care
Residents in the facility are reimbursed at the flat contracted rate with Neighborhood Health.

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational
policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a
sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

           a. Resident’s physical environment:
                  i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                    The Facility provides private and semi-private apartments, spacious rooms, and
                    private bathrooms. While providing that home-like setting, the Facility also
                    provides comfortable common and lounge areas to gather with friends and
                    family as well as a dining room with restaurant-style dining. There are also
                    activity rooms and fitness rooms, as well as gardens and a courtyard.

                  ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                    Every resident may personalize their room with their own items.

                 iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community
                      kitchen(s), laundry, activities;

                    As set forth above, the Facility provides a wide range of activities, including
                    wellness and fitness opportunities. Laundry service is provided to residents.
                    The Facility provides a variety of dining options, including a café.

                 iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and
                     gardening);

                    The Facility is located in a comfortable suburban setting so there are many
                    opportunities for access to the outdoors and outdoor activities. The Facility
                    offers a wide array of activities, including activities taking place outdoors. It
                    also maintains gardens and a courtyard for residents’ enjoyment.

           b. Resident-centered systems of care:
                  i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and
                     negotiated risk;

                    While residents maintain autonomy, the Facility still maintains appropriate
                    security systems. Specifically, the Applicant will ensure that a physical security
                    system, including wander management systems on main exits and alarms on
                    egress doors are operational.

                  ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);




                                                      18

===== PAGE 22 =====
        The Applicant works with residents to create their preferred daily schedules.
        The residents are also able to schedule their daily activities throughout the day.

      iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

        Residents are able to provide their preferred dining location, time of day, and
        meal preferences. The dietary staff will ensure that residents with diet
        restrictions can enjoy a number of different meal choices.

      iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

        The Facility maintains an activity program that provides for a wide array of
        activities for residents. Residents may also participate in their own activities
        and have access to books, movies, games, and other materials. The Applicant
        will always be open to and encourage resident comments on the offered
        activities.

c. Workforce administration:
      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident
         services and foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will maintain the appropriate and required staffing ratios on all
       shifts and in all units. It will ensure that the staffing ratios take into account staff
       capabilities, as well as the needs of each resident. The Applicant will consistently
       monitor the census and residents’ conditions to ensure appropriate staff ratios.

      ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g.
          Registered nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

        The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through financial incentives and
        encouraging job satisfaction. The Applicant will ensure that its staff recognizes
        that they are a very important part of each resident’s life.

                         OPERATIONS TRANSFER AGREEMENT

       This OPERATIONS TRANSFER AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is entered into this
20th day of December 2021 (the “Effective Date”) by and between South County SNF Operations
LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (“Old Operator”), and South County Eden
Operations LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (“New Operator”).

                                         WITNESSETH:

       WHEREAS, 780 Oak Hill Road SNF Real Estate LLC, a Delaware limited liability
company (“Seller”) and 780 Oak Hill Road Eden Realty LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability
company (“Purchaser”) have entered into that certain Asset Purchase Agreement (the “APA”),
dated as of the date hereof, pursuant to which Purchaser will purchase that certain real property
improved with a 120 licensed bed skilled nursing facility located at 740 Oak Hill Road, North
Kingstown, Rhode Island (the “Facility”), commonly known as “South County Nursing and
Rehabilitation Center” (the “Property”);

        WHEREAS, under that certain Consent Agreement effective June 30, 2020 by and
amongst Rhode Island Department of Health (“DOH”), Old Operator, and the Seller (“Consent
Agreement”), Old Operator currently has the sole rights to act as operator of the Facility and wishes
to assign such rights to New Operator;

       WHEREAS, Old Operator currently owns certain furniture, fixtures and equipment,
vehicles and other items of personal property, including as located on, used in connection with,
the operation of the Facility (the “Personal Property”);

         WHEREAS, prior to the Management Transfer Date (as defined below), New Operator
will file its Change of Ownership Application with the DOH and the 855A form with the fiscal
intermediary for the Facility, (collectively, the “CHOW”) pursuant to which New Operator will
obtain its own license to operate the Facility as of the Transition Date (as defined below) and
obtain all rights to the Permits, as defined herein.
        WHEREAS, New Operator and Old Operator have further agreed that New Operator will
manage the Facility for Old Operator from the Management Transfer Date to the Transition Date.
In conjunction therewith, New Operator and Old Operator will enter into an Interim Management
Agreement, the form of which is attached hereto as “Exhibit A” and incorporated herein by this
reference (the “Management Agreement”), and Interim Sublease, the form of which is attached
hereto as “EXHIBIT B” and incorporated herein by this reference (the “Sublease”).
        WHEREAS, in order to ensure an orderly transition of operations of the Facility, the
parties hereto desire to enter into this Agreement.

      NOW, THEREFORE, for the mutual promises and covenants contained herein, and other
good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby mutually
acknowledged by the parties hereto, the parties hereto agree as follows:

            a.      Management Transfer Date. The Old Operator will transfer the management

    Date”) which shall be the date of Closing (as defined under APA) following the satisfaction
    of all conditions precedent as set forth in Section 3 below.

            b.      Transition Date. The Old Operator will transition the operation of the
    Facility to the New Operator (the “Transition”) on the date DOH issues the license to the
    New Operator (the “Transition Date”).

    Agreement, New Operator shall not assume and shall not be liable for, and Old Operator

    of the Facility prior to the Management Transfer Date.

     8.     ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE; ACCOUNTS PAYABLE.

             a.     New Operator shall not assume any accounts receivable owed or due to Old

     accordance with normal business practices and no patients or residents shall be
     unreasonably harassed in the collection of such amounts. Old Operator shall engage
     sufficient personnel to bill and collect Old Operator’s accounts receivable using Old
     Operator’s legacy billing system, which Old Operator shall maintain as required to bill and
     collect its accounts receivable hereunder. New Operator shall allow Old Operator
     reasonable access to the Facility to accomplish these tasks.

             b.     If at any time after the Management Transfer Date, New Operator shall
     receive any payment from any federal or state agency, which payment includes any
     reimbursement with respect to payments or underpayments made to Old Operator for
     services rendered prior to the Management Transfer Date, then New Operator shall remit
     such payments to Old Operator . If at any time after the Management Transfer Date, Old
     Operator shall receive any payment from any federal or state agency, which payment
     represents reimbursement with respect to payments or underpayments made to New
     Operator for services rendered on or after the Management Transfer Date, then Old
     Operator shall remit such payments to New Operator. New Operator and Old Operator
     shall send copies of all Medicare and Medicaid remittance advices to the other party for

     months following the Management Transfer Date and thereafter as reasonably requested
     by each party. Any such remittances pursuant to this Section 8.b. shall occur within fifteen
     (15) days from the date the party required to make such remittance receives payment
     thereof.

             c.      Payments received by New Operator or Old Operator from non-
     governmental payment sources shall be paid to the party designated in such payments
     entitled to the payments for the services provided thereunder on the next to occur of first

     Management Transfer Date provided such date is at least five (5) business days following
14

===== PAGE 79 =====
     receipt of such payment by the party required to make such remittance.

              d.       Any non-designated payments received by New Operator or Old Operator
     for a period of sixty (60) days after the Management Transfer Date shall first be applied to

     provided before the Management Transfer Date, with the excess if any, applied to any post-

     payment shall have no right, title or interest whatsoever in the payment and shall remit the

                          INTERIM MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

        This INTERIM MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT (“Interim Management Agreement,”
or “Agreement”) is entered into effective as of _            (the “Management Transfer
Date”), by and between South County SNF Operations LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability
company (“Operator”) and                                                (“Manager”) and
solely for purposes of Section 12,                                   (“Guarantor”). The
Operator and the Manager are sometimes referred to herein individually as a “Party” and
collectively as the “Parties.”

        WHEREAS, 780 Oak Hill Road SNF Real Estate LLC, a Delaware limited liability
company           (“Seller”),         an         affiliate        of        Operator         and
                                        (“Landlord”), an affiliate of Operator, entered into that
certain Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of                           , 2021 (collectively, the
“APA”), pursuant to which Seller agreed to sell certain assets including real property and
improvements used in connection with that certain skilled nursing facility commonly known as
“South County Nursing and Rehabilitation Center” (the “Facility”) (said real property, including
the land and all improvements thereon, is referred to herein as the “Premises”) to Landlord, and
Operator intends to transfer the operations of the Facility to Manager pursuant to that certain
Operations Transfer Agreement, by and between Operator and Manager, dated as of
                            , 2021 (the “OTA”);

WHEREAS, as of the Closing Date (as defined in the APA), under a lease, Landlord is leasing
the Premises to Manager, as tenant (the “Lease”);

WHEREAS, under a Consent Agreement (as defined in the OTA), Operator currently holds a
certain skilled nursing facility license necessary for the operation of the Facility;

WHEREAS, Manager is in the process of obtaining its own skilled nursing facility license from
the Rhode Island Department of Health, but has not yet received such licensure as of the
Management Transfer Date;

WHEREAS, Manager is entering into a sublease of the Premises with Operator (the “Sublease”),
so that Operator’s license can allow the Facility to remain in operation until such time as Manager
obtains a skilled nursing facility license in its name; and

WHEREAS, Operator and Manager wish to enter into this Interim Management Agreement
whereby, for the duration of the time period necessary for licensing and other regulatory approvals
necessary for Manager to operate the Facility, Manager will manage the Facility in anticipation of
Manager’s receipt of its license to operate the Facility.

       NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt of sufficiency of
which are mutually agreed, and the mutual covenants herein contained, the parties hereto agree as
follows:

===== PAGE 105 =====
        1.      Management. Operator hereby appoints the Manager as manager of the Facility
effective on the Management Transfer Date. Effective on the Management Transfer Date, Manager
agrees to operate and manage the Facility as agent for the Operator, at the Operator’s direction and
subject to that Operator’s control.

        2.      Term and Termination. The term of this Interim Management Agreement will
commence on the Management Transfer Date and will end on the earlier of the following: (a) the
date of Manager’s receipt of a license, (b) the date that Operator’s current license is revoked or
terminated, or (c) mutual written agreement of the Parties, (d) by Operator any time following two
(2) years after the Management Transfer Date unless there is a moratorium or delay by the state,
at which time the allotted period gets extended for up to one (1) additional year (the “Term”)
following which Manager shall have the option to purchase the membership interests of Operator
for $1, subject to applicable law. Manager shall also have the right to terminate this Interim
Management Agreement, upon written notice to Operator, if Operator breaches or fails to perform
any of its duties or obligations under this Interim Management Agreement and such breach or
failure to perform remains uncured to the reasonable satisfaction of Manager for a period of ten
(10) days after Manager provides written notice of such breach or failure to perform to Operator;
provided that in lieu of termination, upon breach of this Agreement by Operator, Manager shall be
entitled to seek an action for specific performance. The date of termination as provided above is
herein referred to as the “Termination Date.” The period commencing on the Management
Transfer Date and terminating on the Termination Date is referred to hereinafter as the
“Management Period”. This Interim Management Agreement may not be amended or modified
except in writing, upon the prior written consent of Landlord and signed by Operator and Manager.

       3.      Compensation and Facility Expenses.

(a)    For its services provided under Section 1, Manager shall be entitled to a fee from the
Operator (the “Management Fee”) equal to the Facility’s net operating revenues during the
Management Period.

(b)     The Manager shall pay all expenses, costs, and charges (including capital outlays) incurred
in the ordinary course in connection with the operation and maintenance of the Facility during the
Management Period, and, subject to the terms of the OTA, Manager shall be entitled to retain and
enjoy all revenues of any nature whatsoever generated from the operation of the Facility during
the Management Period.

(c)     In the event that Manager is not permitted under applicable law to direct the Facility’s gross
revenue to its own bank accounts, Manager and Operator shall jointly maintain the bank accounts
relating to the Facility for one hundred and twenty (120) days after the Management Transfer Date
(the “Initial Period”), to deposit all of the Facility’s gross revenue therein and to pay all Facility
expenses therefrom. After the Initial Period, Manager shall be authorized as agent on behalf of
Operator to solely, maintain the bank accounts relating to the Facility for the Term of this
Agreement, to deposit all of the Facility’s gross revenue therein and to pay all Facility expenses
therefrom. Operator shall have view access of the bank accounts after the Initial Period. As of the
Management Transfer Date, Manager’s representatives shall be listed as signatories on all Facility
bank accounts.

===== PAGE 106 =====
        4.      Operations. During the Management Period, Manager agrees to keep and maintain
the Facility in accordance with all applicable regulations and consistent with commercially
reasonable, good business and industry practices, but in no event in a standard less than the
standard by which such Manager’s affiliates manage their own skilled nursing facilities. Subject
to conditions prescribed in Section 6 herein, Operator agrees to provide the Manager with
undisturbed access to the Facility during the Management Period. Manager will immediately notify
the Operator of any material violations of state and federal laws, rules and regulations. Operator
will use best efforts to keep the license and all Medicare and Medicaid certifications and other
licenses, permits, certifications, and approvals to operate the Facility in good standing throughout
the Management Period. The Parties acknowledge and agree that Manager shall be the exclusive
representative of Operator for purposes of communicating and dealing with the regulatory
authorities, governmental agencies, employees, independent contractors, suppliers, patients,
customers and guests of the Facility. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in any instance in which
Operator is required to perform any obligations or responsibilities as the holder of the skilled
nursing facility license under applicable law, Manager shall cooperate with and take direction from
Operator, to the extent required for Operator to perform its obligations and responsibilities and
have such control as is required by the holder of the existing skilled nursing facility license.

        5.       Operator Status. Operator will at all times during the Management Period continue
to be qualified to be licensed as a skilled nursing facility operator and to be certified by the U.S.
Department of Health and Human Services or the applicable agencies in the state in which the
Facility is located as a provider of services under the Medicare and Medicaid programs. Manager
shall be responsible for any liabilities, costs, damages, losses and expenses of the Facility arising
and attributable to the operation of the applicable Facility during the Management Period (the
“Operating Liabilities”). Manager may pay, when due, any Operating Liabilities from cash flow
arising from or attributable to the operations of the Facility during the Management Period (the
“Contract Term Cash Flow”). Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Contract Term Cash Flow is
not sufficient to satisfy and discharge in full such Operating Liabilities, the Manager shall be
required to so satisfy and discharge such Operating Liabilities, when due, from a Manager’s own
funds. In the event Contract Term Cash Flow exceeds Operating Liabilities, Manager shall be
entitled to retain such excess funds.

       6.      Manager Status.

A.     During the term of this Agreement, the Manager shall not

a) make any material changes to the operations of the Facility without the approval of the Operator,
not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed;

b) have the authority to:

                   a) hire or fire the Chief Executive Officer of the Facility,
                   b) maintain and control the books and records of the Facility,
                   c) dispose of assets and incur liabilities on behalf of the Facility, or
                   d) adopt and enforce policies regarding operation of the Facility.

B. During the term of this Agreement, the Manager shall take all actions necessary for the Facility

===== PAGE 107 =====
to continue to be qualified as a skilled nursing facility.

        7.      Insurance. Operator will maintain all existing insurance coverage held by them
prior to the Management Transfer Date during the Management Period, provided however,
Manager shall be responsible for the payment of the premiums associated with such coverage.
During the Management Period, the Manager shall maintain insurance coverage for the operations
of the Facility consistent with, and not duplicative of, the insurance coverages required to be held
by operators of skilled nursing facilities by applicable law and by the Manager’s lender.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, during the Management Period the Operator shall not make any
claims on its insurance policies with respect to the Management Period without the prior written
consent of the Manager, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned.

        8.     No Covenants or Restrictions. During the Management Period, neither Party will
enter into or cause the imposition of any covenants or restrictions concerning or affecting the
Facility that would have a material adverse effect upon revenues from the Facility or would
prohibit or limit Operator from operating or Manager from managing the Facility in a manner
consistent with applicable laws, rules, and regulations and normal business practices of an operator
and manager, respectively.

        9.     Access to Records. Manager agrees to provide the Operator, during the
Management Period, with copies of all reports or other filings with and communications from all
governmental authorities or agencies having jurisdiction over the Facility. Upon request, Manager
agrees to give Operator or Operator’s representatives access to all such records pertaining to the
Facility, which records will be kept at the Facility. After the Termination Date, Operator will grant
the Manager access to records, reports, communications, and similar documents for the
Management Period in accordance with the OTA.

        10.    Indemnification. The indemnification provisions set forth in Section 14 if the OTA
are incorporated herein by reference thereto.

        11.    Confidential Records; Business Associate Agreement. Manager and the Operator
agree that during the Management Period, Manager shall comply at all times with all applicable
HIPAA rules and regulations with regard to the Facility’s patient records, and will not use or
disclose any Protected Health Information (“PHI”) received, viewed or accessed by the Manager.
Confidentiality of Facility records shall be maintained and protected under the terms of a separate
Business Associate Addendum entered into between Manager and Operator, attached hereto as
“Exhibit A”.

        12.    Guarantee of the Managers’ Indemnification Obligations. As an inducement to the
Operator to enter into and consummate the transactions contemplated under this Agreement, the
Guarantor, hereby, jointly, severally, absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably guarantees to
the Operator all indemnification obligations of Manager under this Agreement (the “Guaranteed
Obligations”). The Guarantor agrees that performance of the Guaranteed Obligations by the
Guarantor shall be a primary obligation, and shall not be subject to any counterclaim, set-off,
abatement, deferment or defense based upon any claim that the Guarantor may have against
Operator. The Guarantor agrees that performance of the Guaranteed Obligations by the Guarantor
shall remain in full force and effect without regard to, and shall not be released, discharged or

===== PAGE 108 =====
affected in any way by, any circumstance or condition (whether or not the Guarantor shall have
any knowledge thereof), including, without limitation, (i) any voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy,
assignment for the benefit of creditors, receivership, or similar events or proceedings with respect
to Manager or the Guarantor, as applicable, or (ii) any other occurrence, circumstance, happening
or event, whether similar or dissimilar to the foregoing and whether foreseen or unforeseen, which
otherwise might constitute a legal or equitable defense or discharge of the liabilities of Guarantor
or which otherwise might limit recourse against an Manager or the Guarantor, to the fullest extent
permitted by law. For so long as this guarantee remains in effect, Guarantor shall not transfer,
lease, assign, sell or convey substantially all of his, her or its assets or cease operating his, her, or
its business in the ordinary course without the prior written consent of a Operator unless Guarantor
is replaced with another guarantor to the Operator’s reasonable satisfaction; provided, such
replacement guarantor has a substantially similar net worth to Guarantor. Guarantor understands
that Operator is relying on this guarantee in entering into this Agreement.

       13.    Governing Law. This Agreement will be governed by, and construed and enforced
in accordance with, the laws of the State of Rhode Island.

        14.    Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is determined by any court of

       15.     Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed and delivered (including by

Entity”) and Manager (“Business Associate”), and is attached to and made part of the Management
Agreement. Covered Entity and Business Associate are sometimes referred to individually as a
“Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall
have the meanings set forth in the Management Agreement.

                                             RECITALS

A.     The Parties acknowledge that they are required to comply with the Health Insurance
Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and its accompanying regulations as amended from
time to time, including the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Heath Information
(“Privacy Rule”) and the Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic Protected Health
Information (the “Security Rule”), as well as Subtitle D of the Health Information Technology for
Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (“HITECH”) of the American Recovery and
Reinvestment Act and its accompanying regulations, as amended from time to time (collectively,
“HIPAA”).

B.      Covered Entity is a “covered entity,” as defined in HIPAA.

C.      Business Associate is a “business associate” as defined by HIPAA.

D.      Business Associate provides management services to Covered Entity (collectively, the
“Services”) in accordance with the Management Agreement to which this Agreement is attached.
In accordance with the terms of the Interim Management Agreement, Business Associate may use,
disclose, create, receive, maintain, or transmit, as applicable, on behalf of Covered Entity,
protected health information (“PHI”) for purposes of providing the Services.

E.   The Parties desire to conduct their business relationship in a manner consistent with
HIPAA.

NOW THEREFORE, in exchange for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and
sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree to incorporate the forgoing recitals as
rewritten above and further agree as follows:

     1. Definitions. Unless otherwise defined in this Agreement, terms shall have the meanings
        established under HIPAA, including but not limited to 45 CFR §§ 160.103, 164.103,
        164.304 and 164.501.
     2. Permitted Uses and Disclosures by Business Associate. Except as otherwise limited in
        this Agreement, Business Associate may use, access, transmit, maintain, create, request or
        disclose PHI to perform functions, activities, or services for, or on behalf of, Covered

===== PAGE 112 =====
     Entity as specified by the Interim Management Agreement and in a manner that does not
     violate HIPAA or other applicable law, including state privacy and security laws.
3.   Business Associate Obligations.
a.   Use or Disclosure of Information. Business Associate shall not use or disclose PHI other
     than as permitted or required to perform the services described in the Management
     Agreement or as required by law.
b.   Safeguards. Business Associate shall employ administrative, physical and technical
     safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and
     availability of PHI, including, without limitation, appropriate training and discipline of
     Business Associate’s work force and restrictions on access to PHI.
c.   Agents and Subcontractors. Business Associate shall ensure that any agents and
     subcontractors, including business associates to whom PHI is made available pursuant to
     this Agreement agree in a binding contract to the same restrictions, conditions and
     obligations that apply through this Agreement to Business Associate with respect to such
     information. Business Associate further agrees to ensure that any agent, subcontractor or
     business associate to whom it provides electronic protected health information (“ePHI”) or
     creates, receives, maintains, or transmits ePHI agrees to implement reasonable and
     appropriate safeguards to protect ePHI and provides training. Business Associate agrees to
     enter into business associate agreements with its business associates that meet the
     requirements of HIPAA and the provisions of this Agreement, including but not limited to
     notification requirements under Section 3d (entitled “Reporting”).
d.   Reporting. Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity promptly, but no later than
     ten (10) business days following the occurrence of any security incident, privacy violations
     or breach as defined by HIPAA or state law, or access, use or disclosure of PHI not
     provided for by this Agreement or the Management Agreement of which Business
     Associate becomes aware (collectively a “HIPAA Incident”). At the sole expense of
     Business Associate, Business Associate shall comply with all applicable federal and state
     breach notification requirements and shall bear all related costs associated with any HIPAA
     Incident, including but not limited to bearing costs to provide the requisite notifications,
     mitigation efforts and, if applicable, credit reporting protection or other consumer/patient
     protections as may be deemed necessary by Covered Entity. Such report by Business
     Associate to Covered Entity shall be in writing and include at least the following
     information:
                        i.  The identity of all the affected individual(s);
                       ii.  PHI or ePHI that is known to be the subject of the HIPAA Incident,
                            including not limited to a description of what information was
                            disclosed, accessed, used, modified or destroyed;
                      iii. The date and time of the HIPAA Incident and when it was
                            discovered by Business Associate and others;

===== PAGE 113 =====
                       iv.   How the information was breached, transmitted or inappropriately
                             accessed, used or disclosed, including facts detailing the HIPAA
                             Incident and parties involved;
                        v.   The persons who are known to have information about HIPAA
                             Incident;
                       vi.   What is being done to and mitigate harm to the affected individual
                             and protect against any further security incidents, privacy violations
                             and breaches; and
                      vii.   Any other known facts and circumstances related to the HIPAA
                             Incident.

Business Associate shall further provide evidence of such required notification compliance upon
written request of Covered Entity and shall cooperate with any investigation, requests for follow
up information and reporting obligation related to a HIPAA Incident.

   e. Access. Business Associate shall cooperate with Covered Entity and act in a manner that
      permits Covered Entity to permit individuals (or personal representatives, as applicable)
      access to PHI in accordance with HIPAA, specifically 45 CFR §164.524. Within ten (10)
      business days of receipt of a written request from Covered Entity, Business Associate shall
      provide access to PHI to Covered Entity or, if directed by Covered Entity, to an individual
      (or personal representative, if applicable) in order to comply with the individual’s right to
      access PHI.
   f. Amendment. Business Associate shall cooperate with Covered Entity and act in a manner
      that permits Covered Entity to make amendments to PHI in accordance with HIPAA,
      specifically 45 CFR §164.526. Within ten (10) business days of receipt of a written request
      from Covered Entity, Business Associate shall amend PHI consistent with the written
      request from Covered Entity.
   g. Accounting of Disclosures. Business Associate shall act in a manner that permits Covered
      Entity to provide an accounting of disclosures to individuals (or personal representatives,
      as applicable) accordance with HIPAA, specifically 42 CFR §164.528. Business Associate
      agrees to document such disclosures of PHI and information related to such disclosures as
      would be required by or for Covered Entity to respond to a request by an individual (or
      personal representative, as applicable) for an accounting of disclosures. Business Associate
      agrees to provide to Covered Entity or an individual, in time and manner as agreed to by
      the Parties, but no later than ten (10) business days, information collected in accordance
      with this Agreement to permit Covered Entity to respond to a request by an individual for
      an accounting of disclosures. If an individual makes a request for an accounting of
      disclosures directly to Business Associate, Business Associate shall provide notice to
      Covered Entity within five (5) business days to allow for Covered Entity to determine
      compliance with this Section 3g.

===== PAGE 114 =====
h. Mitigation. Business Associate shall promptly mitigate any harmful effect resulting from
   use or disclosure of PHI by Business Associate, or its agents, subcontractors or business
   associates, in violation of the requirements of this Agreement, and immediately notify
   Covered Entity in writing of such mitigation efforts.
i. Cure of Noncompliance. If Covered Entity notifies Business Associate that a pattern of
   activity or practice of Business Associate constitutes a material breach or violation of this
   Agreement or HIPAA, Business Associate shall immediately take reasonable steps to cure
   the breach or end the violation.
j. Minimum Necessary. Covered Entity will provide, and Business Associate will request,
   no more than the minimum necessary amount of PHI required for the performance of
   Business Associate’s services under the Management Agreement.
k. Sale of PHI. Business Associate shall not directly or indirectly receive remuneration in
   exchange for any PHI of an individual unless Covered Entity has provided Business
   Associate with a valid authorization under HIPAA from each individual whose information
   is the subject of the remuneration transaction or unless Covered Entity has approved such
   remuneration transaction in writing consistent with HIPAA.
l. Training. Business Associate shall provide reasonable education and training on all
   aspects of HIPAA to all agents, subcontractors and member of its workforce.
m. Cooperation with Investigations. Business Associate shall make all internal practices,
   books, records, and agreements with subcontractors, business associates and agents
   relating to the use and disclosure of received or maintained pursuant to this Agreement or
   services provided under the Management Agreement available to Covered Entity and/or
   the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services (“Secretary”) for purposes of
   determining Covered Entity’s and/or Business Associate’s compliance with HIPAA.
   Business Associate shall designate an individual or individuals with authority in the area
   of HIPAA compliance to assist with the investigations and reporting obligations under this
   Agreement.
n. Government Subpoenas. Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity immediately but
   not later than five (5) business days of Business Associate’s receipt of any government
   request or subpoena for PHI with purpose of providing Covered Entity enough time to
   dispute or challenge the request or subpoena authority for such records or other
   information. To the extent that Covered Entity decides to assume responsibility for
   challenging the validity of such request, Business Associate agrees to cooperate fully with
   Covered Entity in such challenge.
o. Books and Records. Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books, and
   records available to the Secretary for purposes of determining compliance with HIPAA.



p. Privacy Rule. To the extent that Business Associate is to carry out one or more of Covered
   Entity’s obligations under the Privacy Rule, Business Associate shall comply with the

===== PAGE 115 =====
        requirements of the Privacy Rule that apply to the Covered Entity in the performance of
        such obligations.
   q.   Indemnification. Business Associate agrees to indemnify and hold Covered Entity, and
        all employees, officers, directors, representatives and agents of Covered Entity, harmless
        from and against any and all liability and costs, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, arising
        from a violation of HIPAA or a material breach of this Agreement by Business Associate
        or its agents, subcontractors, workforce members, business associates, directors and
        officers. This Section 3q shall survive expiration or termination of this Agreement.
   4.   Term and Termination.
   a.   Term. This Agreement shall be on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and
        effect until the effective date of the termination, cancellation, expiration or other
        conclusion of the Management Agreement or termination of this Agreement under this
        Section 4.
   b.   Termination. Covered Entity may immediately terminate this Agreement as follows:

i.     Upon Covered Entity’s knowledge of a material breach by Business Associate, Covered
Entity shall provide Business Associate with written notice of the breach, after which time
Business Associate shall have a period of thirty (30) days to cure the breach or end the violation.
Thereafter, Covered Entity may terminate the Management Agreement if Business Associate does
not cure the breach or end the violation within such thirty (30) day period.

ii.     In the event that Business Associate becomes aware of a pattern of activity or a practice of
Covered Entity that constitutes a material breach of the obligations of Covered Entity under this
Agreement, Business Associate will provide Covered Entity with the opportunity to cure any such
breach of this Agreement within thirty (30) days of written notice from Business Associate
detailing such pattern.

   c. Effect of Termination. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, Business
      Associate shall promptly return to Covered Entity or destroy all PHI received from, or
      created or received on behalf of, Covered Entity (including all copies) in the possession or
      control of Business Associate and its subcontractors, agents and business associates.
      Destruction of PHI shall be by HIPAA compliant means approved by Covered Entity and
      Business Associate sending written certification of destruction to Covered Entity within
      ten (10) days of such destruction. If return or destruction of PHI is not feasible, as
      reasonably determined by Business Associate, Business Associate shall provide Covered
      Entity with written notice in which Business Associate describes why return or destruction
      is not feasible, and Business Associate shall thereafter extend the protections of this
      Agreement to the PHI and limit further uses and disclosures to those purposes that make
      return or destruction infeasible.

                               INTERIM SUBLEASE AGREEMENT

This INTERIM SUBLEASE AGREEMENT (this “Sublease”) is made and entered into as of
                      , 2021 (the “Effective Date”) by and among South County SNF
Operations LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (the “Tenant”) and
                           (the “Landlord”).

Landlord is the lessee of the skilled nursing facility located at 740 Oak Hill Road, North
Kingstown, Rhode Island and commonly known as South County Nursing and Rehabilitation
Center     (the    “Facility”).         Landlord      is     leasing   the     Facility    from
                                                    under a certain Nursing Home Lease
Agreement (the “Master Lease”). As used herein, the term the “Facility” refers to the real
property described above, all improvements located on that real property, and the fixtures,
furnishings, equipment and other personal property used in the management and operation thereof.

Landlord has applied for a new license and/or other required approvals to operate the Facility as a
skilled nursing facility (the “New License”) from the Rhode Island Department of Health
(“DOH”). Until the New License is issued to Landlord by DOH, Landlord desires for Tenant to
remain in legal possession of the Facility so that Tenant’s license to operate the Facility will remain
in effect.

Tenant is currently the licensed operator of the Facility pursuant to its existing license and/or other
required approvals from DOH (the “Existing License”).

Pending the issuance of the New License, Landlord desires to sublease the Facility to Tenant, and
Tenant desires to sublease the Facility from Landlord, for the purpose of providing for the
continued operation of the Facility under the Existing License as provided in this Sublease and the
Management Agreement (as defined below).

Landlord and Tenant have entered into an Interim Management Agreement (the “Management
Agreement”), pursuant to which Landlord shall manage the Facility under Tenant’s Existing
License during the term of the Management Agreement. If there is any conflict between the terms
of the Management Agreement and this Sublease, the terms of the Management Agreement shall
control.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the covenants and conditions contained herein, and for
other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby
acknowledged, the parties hereby agree as follows:

       1.      SUBLEASE OF THE FACILITY:

Landlord does hereby sublease to Tenant, and Tenant does hereby sublease from Landlord, the
Facility. The Facility shall be hereinafter referred to as the “Leased Premises.” Tenant hereby
agrees to act as “subtenant” of the Leased Premises during the Sublease Term (as defined below)
for the purpose of allowing Tenant, under the Existing License, to continue to operate the Facility
with and through Landlord as the Leased Premises’ manager, maintaining ownership of resident

===== PAGE 118 =====
agreements and records as required by applicable law, and performing any other non-delegable
duties of Tenant under applicable law.

      2.       TERM; TERMINATION:

2.1    Term. The term of this Sublease (the “Sublease Term”) shall commence on the Effective
Date and shall continue for a term coterminous with the term of the Management Agreement unless
this Sublease terminates pursuant to Section 2.2 below or terminates on account of a default by
Tenant.

2.2     Termination. This Sublease shall terminate automatically without the need for further
action or the execution of any further documents by any of the parties hereto, upon the earlier of
(a) the date on which the New License is issued to Landlord or (b) earlier termination of the
Management Agreement by Tenant.

      3.       PAYMENTS BY TENANT:

Commencing on the Effective Date, Tenant shall pay to Landlord as rent for the Leased Premises
the sum of Twelve Dollars ($12.00) for the entire Sublease Term in one lump sum payment payable
in advance.

      4.       PAYMENTS BY LANDLORD:

4.1     Utilities. Landlord shall pay all water, gas, heat, light, power, telephone service and all
other utility services supplied to the Leased Premises during the Sublease Term.

4.2    Taxes. Landlord shall pay all real and personal property taxes, assessments and levies of
any kind or nature whatsoever taxed, assessed, levied or imposed upon or against the Leased
Premises during the Sublease Term.

4.3     Insurance. Landlord shall pay all insurance premiums for all insurance coverage required
of the Landlord as a lessee under the Master Lease. Landlord covenants and agrees that all of the
property constituting the Leased Premises is covered as of the date hereof and will be covered at
all times by general liability, fire, theft and property damage insurance. All such insurance shall
name Landlord and Tenant as insureds as their respective interests may appear.

4.4     Repairs and Maintenance; Alterations. Landlord shall pay all costs of repairing and
maintaining the Leased Premises and every part thereof in good and sanitary order, condition and
repair during the term hereof, reasonable wear and tear excepted. Tenant shall not make any
alterations or changes to the Leased Premises without the prior written approval of Landlord in its
sole discretion.

      5.       USE:

Tenant shall use the Leased Premises for the continued operation of a skilled nursing facility under
the Existing License, with and through Landlord as the manager of the Leased Premises pending
the issuance of the New License to Landlord. Landlord agrees to devote its reasonable best efforts
toward obtaining the New License.

===== PAGE 119 =====
      6.          ASSIGNMENT:

                Tenant’s rights and obligations under this Sublease may not be assigned
(collaterally or otherwise) or further sublet, or otherwise transferred in whole or in part, without
the prior written consent of Landlord.

      7.          INDEMNIFICATION:

       Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Sublease (but without limiting
any provisions of the Management Agreement):

               7.1     Tenant shall defend, indemnify, hold harmless and reimburse Landlord, its
members, officers, directors, shareholders, affiliates, representatives and advisors from and against
any and all demands, claims, losses, liabilities, actions, proceedings and expenses (including,
without limitation, reasonable attorneys’ fees) (“Losses”) incurred by any of the foregoing
(whether incurred during the Sublease Term or thereafter) and arising from Tenant’s gross
negligence, willful misconduct or breach of its obligations under this Sublease.

                 7.2     Landlord shall defend, indemnify, hold harmless and reimburse Tenant, its
members, officers, directors, shareholders, affiliates, representatives and advisors, from and
against any and all Losses incurred by any of the foregoing and arising out of (a) the ownership,
management or operation of the Leased Premises during the Sublease Term and/or (b) any breach
by Landlord of this Sublease, to the extent, in the case of each of subsections (a) and (b) above,
that such Losses are not attributable to the gross negligence, willful misconduct or breach of Tenant
in respect to its obligations under this Sublease.

               7.3     The provisions of this Section 7 shall survive the expiration or earlier
termination of this Sublease.

      8.          NOTICES

               All notices or other communications pursuant to this Sublease shall be in writing
and shall be deemed to be sufficient if (a) delivered personally, (b) sent by nationally recognized,
overnight courier, (c) sent or mailed by registered or certified mail (return receipt requested),
postage prepaid, or (d) sent by electronic transmission, to the parties specified below at the
following addresses (or at such other address for a party as shall be specified by like notice):

                  If to Tenant:

      9.       ENTIRE AGREEMENT; MODIFICATION; WAIVER

                This Sublease, together with the other agreements referred to herein and executed
in conjunction herewith, constitutes the entire understanding between the parties with respect to
the express subject matter hereof, superseding all negotiations, prior discussions and preliminary
agreements. This Sublease may not be modified or amended except in writing signed by the parties

                               INTERIM SUBLEASE AGREEMENT

This INTERIM SUBLEASE AGREEMENT (this “Sublease”) is made and entered into as of
March 1, 2022 (the “Effective Date”) by and among South County SNF Operations LLC, a
Rhode Island limited liability company (the “Tenant”) and South County Eden Operations LLC,
a Rhode Island limited liability company (the “Landlord”).

Landlord is the lessee of the skilled nursing facility located at 740 Oak Hill Road, North
Kingstown, Rhode Island and commonly known as South County Nursing and Rehabilitation
Center (the “Facility”). Landlord is leasing the Facility from 780 Oak Hill Road Eden Realty
LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company under a certain Nursing Home Lease Agreement
(the “Master Lease”). As used herein, the term the “Facility” refers to the real property described
above, all improvements located on that real property, and the fixtures, furnishings, equipment and
other personal property used in the management and operation thereof.

Landlord has applied for a new license and/or other required approvals to operate the Facility as a
skilled nursing facility (the “New License”) from the Rhode Island Department of Health
(“DOH”). Until the New License is issued to Landlord by DOH, Landlord desires for Tenant to
remain in legal possession of the Facility so that Tenant’s license to operate the Facility will remain
in effect.

Tenant is currently the licensed operator of the Facility pursuant to its existing license and/or other
required approvals from DOH (the “Existing License”).

Pending the issuance of the New License, Landlord desires to sublease the Facility to Tenant, and
Tenant desires to sublease the Facility from Landlord, for the purpose of providing for the
continued operation of the Facility under the Existing License as provided in this Sublease and the
Management Agreement (as defined below).

Landlord and Tenant have entered into an Interim Management Agreement (the “Management
Agreement”), pursuant to which Landlord shall manage the Facility under Tenant’s Existing
License during the term of the Management Agreement. If there is any conflict between the terms
of the Management Agreement and this Sublease, the terms of the Management Agreement shall
control.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the covenants and conditions contained herein, and for
other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby
acknowledged, the parties hereby agree as follows:

       1.      SUBLEASE OF THE FACILITY:

Landlord does hereby sublease to Tenant, and Tenant does hereby sublease from Landlord, the
Facility. The Facility shall be hereinafter referred to as the “Leased Premises.” Tenant hereby
agrees to act as “subtenant” of the Leased Premises during the Sublease Term (as defined below)
for the purpose of allowing Tenant, under the Existing License, to continue to operate the Facility
with and through Landlord as the Leased Premises’ manager, maintaining ownership of resident
agreements and records as required by applicable law, and performing any other non-delegable
duties of Tenant under applicable law.

===== PAGE 137 =====
      2.       TERM; TERMINATION:

2.1    Term. The term of this Sublease (the “Sublease Term”) shall commence on the Effective
Date and shall continue for a term coterminous with the term of the Management Agreement unless
this Sublease terminates pursuant to Section 2.2 below or terminates on account of a default by
Tenant.

2.2     Termination. This Sublease shall terminate automatically without the need for further
action or the execution of any further documents by any of the parties hereto, upon the earlier of
(a) the date on which the New License is issued to Landlord or (b) earlier termination of the
Management Agreement by Tenant.

      3.       PAYMENTS BY TENANT:

      4.       PAYMENTS BY LANDLORD:

                                 Sunny View Nursing Home, Inc.

                                        Charity Care Policy

1.      Purpose. It shall be the policy of Sunny View Nursing Home, Inc.,
("Provider") to provide free care to certain Qualifying Patients as outlined herein, in Provider's
discretion.

2.      Qualifying Patients. Provider may make free care available to those patients otherwise
medically eligible for Provider's services that also meet the charity care guidelines as outlined
herein ("Qualifying Patients"). Accordingly, Qualifying Patients will be those uninsured patients
with family incomes up to 125% of the Federal Poverty Limits and limited assets. Qualifying
Patients must have applied for any governmental assistance programs for which they qualify. If a
Qualifying Patient is not eligible for governmental assistance or is denied governmental
assistance, such patient may apply for charity care.

3.      Charity Care Policy. Provider agrees it will neither bill Qualifying Patients for services
directly supplied by Provider nor collect any fees for provision of such services. Services that are
provided under contract with an outside provider shall not be eligible for charity care and will be
billed in the customary manner.

4.     Monitoring. An annual summary of charity care will be drafted and provided to the
Provider's management on an annual basis.

Title: Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement Plan

Policy: To outline a standard format for Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement
which is proactive and continually improves the way the facility cares for and engages residents,
caregivers and other partners. All employees will participate in ongoing improvement activities
in support of the performance improvement mission.

Guiding Principles:

1. Quality Assessment/Performance Improvement (QAPI) has a prominent role in our
management functions.

2. Our organization uses QAPI to make decisions and guide day to day operations.

The outcome of our QAPI program is to improve the quality of life and quality of care for

our residents.

4. QAPI includes all departments, all employees and all services.

QAPI focuses on systems and processes, rather than individuals.

6. Our organization makes decisions based on data. We set goals for performance and
measure our progress.

7. Our culture supports, rather than punishes employees who identify errors.

ed

ms

Design/Scope:

QAPI is ongoing and comprehensive. Activities are directed by the QAPI committee. All
systems of care will be addressed in the program, with a focus on clinical care, quality of life and
resident choice. Safety and quality are a key element of all activities. Evidenced based practice
will be researched and incorporated.

Governance and Leadership:

QAPI activities. Leadership will assure that adequate resources are dedicated to the QAPI
activities. The Quality Assurance Coordinator is designated overall responsibility for the plan
and activities. Training will be provided to staff regarding the QAPI plan, performance
improvement activities and tools. Staff will have time, equipment and technical training needed
to participate in activities. Leadership will assure that QAPI is a priority and assist in setting
expectations around quality, safety, rights and choices. Leadership is responsible for creating an
atmosphere where staff are comfortable identifying and reporting quality problems and
opportunities for improvement.

Facility Administration will develop a Fa that involves staff, resident and family input into

Feedback, Data Systems and Monitoring:

Data will drive all performance tngreyenent activities. Monitoring will occur in each
department to track compliance, identify improvement opportunities and assure that the facility
is meeting or exceeding standards of care practice. Feedback will be obtained from staff,
residents, families and vendors. Performance Indicators will be selected for monitoring each
year. They will be evaluated annually, Results will be analyzed and trended against benchmarks
both internal and external. Goals for improvement will be developed and tracked. Tracking and
investigating outlying areas will be accomplished utilizing proven Quality Assurance

===== PAGE 152 =====
[OCR]
methodologies, i.e. Event flow diagrams, root cause analysis etc. Plans will be developed to
address Adverse Events. The facility utilizes the plan/do/check/act methodology.

’ Performance Improvement Projects:

A performance Improvement Project (PIP) is a concentrated effort in a problem area. It will
involve chartering a team, gathering information, clarifying the issue and proposing solutions.
The QA Coordinator is responsible for chartering the teams and assisting them in the process.
All teams will report results thru the QAPI Committee. The facility conducts PIPs to examine
and improve care or services in areas that the facility identifies as needing attention.

System Analysis and Action:

The facility utilizes a systematic approach to determine when an in-depth analysis is needed to
fully understand a problem, its cause and the implications of change. A QAPI Self-Assessment
will be performed annually to determine the progress with QAPI initiatives. A Performance
Improvement Criteria Checklist will be used to determine if a PIP will be chartered. Once the
decision to charter a team is made, the QA Coordinator will identify a team leader for the process
and assist in selecting members and working with the team throughout the process. Policies and
procedures will be developed to outline the process for Root Cause Analysis and Annual Review
of the QAPI plan. All systems will eventually be comprehensively reviewed in an effort to
prevent future adverse events and promote sustained improvement.

Quality Assurance Performance Improvement Committee
The QAPI Committee members consist at minimum of:
Administrator
Medical Director
Director of Nursing
Quality Assurance Coordinator
Staff Development
Department Heads
Vendors (including pharmacy)
Front Line Staff representing key departments
The purpose of the committee is to lead the facilities QAPI activities, to identify issues related to

care and services and develop, implement and evaluate plans of action to maintain the quality
and safety of care and to correct identified deficiencies.

The Committee processes will be data driven, and may include monitoring results from:

Title: Root Cause Analysis

Policy: To standardize the format and process for conducting a root cause analysis.

Procedure:

L.

2.

~

10.

A root cause analysis (RCA) will be conducted for any sentinel event. In addition,
department heads may initiate a RCA in any area they deem appropriate.

The definition of a sentinel event is:

Accident that results in death or serious injury of staff, resident or visitor.
Elopement

Fire/Major utility failure

Incident with potential for serious harm (re: resident left at outside appointment
unattended)

e. Any incident the Administrator feels warrants a thorough investigation.

f. Employee injuries which result in lost time.

The Administrator will decide if an incident meets the above definitions. All incidents
that are being investigated via root cause analysis will be forwarded to the Quality
Assurance Coordinator. The QAC will assist with the RCA.

The QAC will appoint a team leader and at least three staff to complete the root cause
investigation. Members of the team will include staff that have direct knowledge of the
process involved with the incident.

The team will be given access to all written information related to the accident/incident
(i.e. witness statements, incidents, reports etc.). They may decide to personally interview
staff members involved.

A cause and effect tool will be used to analyze the incident.

At the conclusion of the review, an analysis of the RCA will be documented in
confidential minutes, signed by the administrator and kept on file in the QAC office.
The team leader will mark the documents included in the investigation
“CONFIDENTIAL: FOR USE BY QUALITY ASSURANCE COMMITTEE ONLY”.
The team will submit documentation and discuss results with the Administrator.

The QAC will assign follow-up|responsibility, assure completion and filed documents.
Reports will be generated to Committees as needed (i.e. Safety) All RCAs will be
reported through the Quality Assurance Committee.

RCA should usually be completed within 2 weeks of an incident. The Administrator may
grant an extension as needed. Submit completed RCA to the QAC.

Care Planning Process

Policy:

The resident-centered, goal oriented care plan process is to be interdisciplinary, realistic,
individualized and utilized on a daily basis to promote quality of care and quality of life for all
residents. The following four-step process is to be used in developing care plans that can assist
staff in helping residents achieve their highest practicable physical, mental and psychosocial
well-being, consistent with resident rights. The steps are:

1. Assessment (Problem, Need, Concern Identified)
2. Planning (Goal Setting)

3. Implementation (Developing Approaches)

4, Evaluation (Evaluating Progress Towards Goal)

The Plan of Care must include measurable objectives and timeframes and describe:

¢ Services to be furnished for resident to achieve their highest practicable physical, mental
and psychosocial well-being.

¢ Any services that would otherwise be required but not provided due to the residents

exercise of rights, including the right to refuse treatment.

Any Specialized Services or specialized rehab based on the PASARR recommendations.

In consult with resident, their:

Goals for admission and desired outcomes

Preferences and potential for future discharge. Facility will address residents’ goals for

returning to the community, along with any referrals made for this purpose.

e Discharge Plans

Assessment

1. The team, as per guidelines will complete a comprehensive interdisciplinary assessment
using the Resident Assessment Instrument specified by CMS along with the following
assessments:

Nursing admission assessment

Nutritional Assessment |

Social Services Assessment)

Discharge Planning Review

Activities Assessment

Rehabilitation Screen/Evaluation

Fall Risk Assessment

AIMS

Psychosocial Assessment

Self-Administration of medication assessment

Wander Risk Assessment

===== PAGE 156 =====
[OCR]
e Smoking Assessment
e Risk Indicator for Behaviors
e Continence Assessment

The facility will document who participated in the assessment. Participation must include direct
communication with the resident and direct care staff. The resident assessments will be
coordinated with the PASARR. The facility will refer all Level II residents and all newly
evident or possible mental disorder, intellectual disability, or related conditions for a level II
review upon a significant change is status assessment. The facility will incorporate
recommendations from the PASARR Level II and PASARR evaluation into the resident’s
assessment, care planning and transitions of care.

2:

The Interdisciplinary Team is to include, but not limited to, The Nurse Manager or

designee, Social Worker, Dietitian, Activities Coordinator, Rehabilitation Representative,

Restorative Nursing Representative, Certified Nursing Assistant, and Resident Family

Representative.

Items triggered on the MDS will have corresponding CAA’s completed.

When a resident experiences a ‘change of status” (refer to the MDS user manual), A new

MDS, CAA’s and revised care plan will be developed.

After an assessment has been completed, each problem is identified, and staff needs to

continue the assessment process until the determined why it is a problem for the resident

or those that provide care to the resident.

The care plan process will specifically address, but is not limited to, the following:

e Resident needs, i.e., functional, medical, psychosocial, spiritual, nutritional, social
and educational.

e Advanced Directive Issues, i.e. unable to make informed decisions on admission to
provide more information.

An interim care plan will be developed within 48 hours of admission, utilizing the

following, but not limited to:

e Nursing Admission Assessment

e Risk Assessments

Care Plans will be updated as new needs/problems/concerns arise, and formally reviewed

by the Interdisciplinary team at least quarterly.

All team members involved in the assessment process need to be sure to assess any

educational needs of the resident and/or family and address on the care plan as needed.

Planning (Goal Setting)

1.

After the need/Concern/Problem list has been developed, goals must be set for each
need/concern/problem, which was identified. Goals must be individualized, measureable,
and attainable and have a time frame. Needs identified from triggered CAAs during the
comprehensive MDS process will be reviewed and care planned as resident status
indicates.

All team members, including the resident and/or family representative, participate in
developing the resident centered goals. Residents and/or Family representative/guardians
will be notified at least two weeks in advance of the care plan meeting date. The

===== PAGE 157 =====
[OCR]
exception to this will be in the incidence of a significant change in status and initial care
plan, but all efforts will be made to offer advanced notice of the meeting as allowed.
The resident will have the right to request meetings, along with the right to request
revisions to the plan of care. The resident has the right to participate in establishing the
expected goals and outcomes of the plan of care along with the type, amount, frequency,
duration of care, and any factors related to the effectiveness off the plan of care.

Implementation

L

Individualized Approaches/Interventions are to be developed that assist the resident to
achieve the stated goals.

2. The Care Plan interventions/approaches are to state the person/discipline responsible for

carrying out the intervention/approach.

Evaluation

1.

Although evaluation is a constant process for all identified goals, a formal review process
must take place at least quarterly. Social Services is responsible for notifying the resident
and responsible party regarding the Care Plan reviews.

Documentation of the care plan meeting is to include, but not limited to, the resident
and/or family representatives’ participation in the process and those attending the care
plan meeting.

Care Plans are placed on a regular schedule with changes being made in conjunction with
the MDS dates. Schedules are distributed monthly at a convenient date so that written
reviews can be completed and notifications can be made in a timely manner.

Other Care Planning Guidelines

1.

2.

The care plan is designed as a tool that is used daily to guide the plan of care for each
resident.

As new problems/concerns occur, the care plan is to be updated as soon as possible. The
Licensed Nurse noting new orders that are relevant to the care plan is responsible for
updating the care plan.

All staff involved in any way with completing resident care must have access to and be
familiar with, the resident care plan.
